The words

Man of Sorrows! what a name
For the Son of God, who came
Ruined sinners to reclaim.
Hallelujah! What a Savior!

Bearing shame and scoffing rude,
In my place condemned He stood;
Sealed my pardon with His blood.

Guilty, vile, and helpless we;
Spotless Lamb of God was He;
"Full atonement!" can it be?

Lifted up was He to die;
"It is finished!" was His cry;
Now in Heav'n exalted high.

When He comes, our glorious King,
All His ransomed home to bring,
Then anew His song we'll sing:

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum C and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (G).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest. A cell split by a comma holds two quarter beats: d -,r is a dotted quaver and a semiquaver, d,r two semiquavers. That comma sits between two syllables; an octave mark sits small and low against its own letter (s,).
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by Philip Paul Bliss, first published in 1875. The tune, HALLELUJAH WHAT A SAVIOR, is by Philip Paul Bliss (1875). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1875): Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876)
  • Music (1875): Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876)

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HALLELUJAH WHAT A SAVIOR by Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876); words by Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876). Questions about Hallelujah, What a Savior!

What is the doh of Hallelujah, What a Savior!?

In this version, in C major, doh is C. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Hallelujah, What a Savior! start on?

It starts on s (G in C major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is Hallelujah, What a Savior! in the public domain?

Yes. Philip Paul Bliss died in 1876, Philip Paul Bliss died in 1876; the words were first published in 1875 and the music in 1875. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
